headline: Charles River: From 'Dirty Water' to America's Cleanest Urban River
meta_description: Six decades of restoration transformed the 80-mile Charles River into America's cleanest urban waterway through dam removals, cleanup, and treatment.
summary_short: Once called 'Dirty Water,' the Charles River became America's cleanest urban river after 60 years of dedicated restoration and climate resilience work.
body:
Once called 'Dirty Water,' the Charles River has been transformed into America's cleanest urban river—a remarkable achievement born from six decades of sustained restoration effort.

The 80-mile river's turnaround involved three key strategies: removing dams, conducting extensive trash cleanup, and upgrading water treatment systems. These efforts addressed the river's core problems at multiple levels, from infrastructure to daily maintenance, creating lasting environmental change.

The Charles River's journey from pollution to pristine waterway demonstrates what's possible when communities commit to long-term environmental stewardship. Climate resilience became part of that mission, ensuring the river doesn't just look cleaner today but remains healthy for generations ahead. The project stands as a model for urban waterway restoration across America.
quick_facts: Charles River spans 80 miles from source to mouth
Six decades of restoration transformed the waterway
Dam removals, cleanup, and water treatment were key strategies
Now recognized as America's cleanest urban river
